name: rootfetch
description: Size, growth, owner and abuse signals for ~1,080 domain extensions (TLDs), from ICANN zone files counted daily.

interface.longDescription:
RootFetch counts the registered domains under about 1,080 generic domain extensions (TLDs) such as .xyz, .shop, .app and .bond, from ICANN's zone files, and publishes the numbers every day.

Ask how big an extension is, who runs it, whether it is growing or shrinking, and what public abuse signals it shows. Compare extensions side by side, rank them by size or growth, see every recorded count for one extension, and find sudden registration bursts, which are often price promotions and sometimes waves of spam or phishing domains.

For people checking an unfamiliar link, domain buyers, security teams and journalists. Limits: .com and country codes such as .uk or .de are not covered; most extensions are re-counted about every two weeks (.xyz, .app and .dev daily); counts can lag or contain errors; abuse signals describe an extension as a whole and say nothing about any single website. Read-only; no account is needed.
defaultPrompt: I got a link ending in .bond. What abuse signals does that extension show?
Which domain extensions are growing fastest right now?

positive.description: Safety and owner of one extension
positive.prompt: Is the .bond domain extension safe, and who runs it?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls lookup_tld with .bond and reports its registered domains and rank (1,183,710, #13 when last tested), that ShortDot SA runs it, and a 'be careful' verdict because it is named in Interisle Consulting Group's abuse reports, with the link to its RootFetch page.

positive.prompt: Which domain extensions with at least 10,000 domains are growing fastest?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls rank_tlds with by=fastest_growing and lists extensions with their weekly growth (.yachts, .express and .motorcycles at 11-13% a week when last tested), with the data date.

positive.prompt: Were there any unusual domain registration jumps in the last two weeks?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls recent_jumps with days=14 and lists each jump with its date, percentage, domains added and severity (for example .express +24.2%, critical, when last tested).
Calls compare_tlds and gives each extension's size, rank, weekly growth, operator and safety verdict (.xyz and .top named in abuse reports, .shop clean when last tested).

positive.prompt: Show me how the number of .dev domains changed this year.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls tld_history with .dev and summarises the recorded counts from February 2026 to the latest check (about 597,000 at the start).
